plain.li: Said the words for {NAME} today. My voice held until the last line, which is further than last year.
Kept the words short for {NAME}, five lines and a silence. Then back to work.
[devout] At the graves for {NAME}, I asked that the dead be kept safe. I believe they are.
[winter] Snow on the graves for {NAME}. I kept it brief, and we stamped our feet through every line.

warm.li: After the rite for {NAME}, people stayed by the graves and told the good stories. I stood at the back and let them.

blunt.li: Kept {NAME}. Short words, every one of them meant.

gloomy.li: A year on, and {NAME} again. I wonder whose name I'll be saying next.

cold.li: Led the rite for {NAME}. Eleven came and two wept. I've noted both, to visit later in the week.

cheerful.li: For {NAME} we told the old stories instead of crying through it, and people laughed. A good day, all told.

plain.li: {PAWN_nameDef}, the chaplain, sat down beside {OTHER_nameDef} and let {OTHER_objective} talk about the one {OTHER_pronoun} lost, without hurrying {OTHER_objective}.
{PAWN_nameDef} found {OTHER_nameDef} alone and walked with {OTHER_objective} round the walls, talking about whatever {OTHER_pronoun} liked.
[devout] {PAWN_nameDef} knelt with {OTHER_nameDef} and prayed for the one {OTHER_pronoun} lost, slowly, so that {OTHER_nameDef} could say the words too.

warm.li: {PAWN_nameDef} brought {OTHER_nameDef} a cup of broth and stayed beside {OTHER_objective} until it was finished, saying very little.

blunt.li: {PAWN_nameDef} made {OTHER_nameDef} no promise that the hurt would pass soon, only that {PAWN_pronoun} would be around for all of it.

cold.li: {PAWN_nameDef} asked {OTHER_nameDef} three plain questions about {OTHER_possessive} grief and listened to every answer without a word.

plain.li: {PAWN_nameDef}, the chaplain, found {OTHER_nameDef} at work and asked how the faith was sitting with {OTHER_objective} these days. They talked until the light went.
{PAWN_nameDef} and {OTHER_nameDef} argued about the faith, good-naturedly and at length, until {OTHER_nameDef} ran out of objections.
{PAWN_nameDef} read {OTHER_nameDef} a passage of the old words and asked what {OTHER_pronoun} made of it.

warm.li: {PAWN_nameDef} spoke to {OTHER_nameDef} of {PAWN_possessive} own years of doubt, and how {PAWN_pronoun} found {PAWN_possessive} way back to the faith.

blunt.li: {PAWN_nameDef} asked {OTHER_nameDef} straight out what was troubling {OTHER_objective} about the faith, and answered every point.

cold.li: {PAWN_nameDef} took {OTHER_nameDef} through the faith's teachings one at a time and asked which of them {OTHER_pronoun} still held.

cheerful.li: {PAWN_nameDef} taught {OTHER_nameDef} a hymn {OTHER_pronoun} had never heard, and they sang it through twice.

plain.li: Long talk with {OTHER_nameDef} about the faith. I said more than I meant to.
I've been drifting from the faith. {OTHER_nameDef} noticed before I did.
{OTHER_nameDef} didn't tell me I was wrong to doubt. That's probably why I listened.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} sat with me and talked about what we believe. Steadier now than I've been in weeks.

blunt.li: Talked with {OTHER_nameDef} about the faith. Fair answers. I'll think about them.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} tried to talk me round. About half of it took.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} made a reasonable case for the faith. I'm less sure of my doubts than I was this morning.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} answered every question I had about the faith, even the silly ones!

plain.li: {PAWN_nameDef}, the warden of guests, sat at the camp's fire with the {PLACE} and heard out their complaints about the boundary, one at a time.
{PAWN_nameDef} ate with the {PLACE} at their camp and traded news: theirs from the road, the colony's from the fields.
{PAWN_nameDef} settled an argument between the {PLACE} and the colony's woodcutters before anyone raised their voice.
[rain] {PAWN_nameDef} sat out the rain under the camp's awning with the {PLACE}, swapping stories about the road.

warm.li: {PAWN_nameDef} went over to the camp to ask how they were getting on there, and stayed long after the question was answered.

blunt.li: {PAWN_nameDef} went to the camp, said the colony's piece, heard the {PLACE} out and came back.

cold.li: {PAWN_nameDef} reminded the {PLACE} of the terms they had agreed to, one by one.

plain.li: {PAWN_nameDef}, the warden of guests, welcomed {OTHER_nameDef} and the rest of the party from {FACTION} and asked after their road. {FACTION} will hear of it.
{PAWN_nameDef} found {OTHER_nameDef} of {FACTION} a seat out of the wind and sat down to hear the news from the road.
{PAWN_nameDef} showed the visitors from {FACTION} round the colony, and {OTHER_nameDef} wanted to know what every building was for.

warm.li: {PAWN_nameDef} greeted {OTHER_nameDef} of {FACTION} by name, like an old friend, and asked how the road had treated {OTHER_objective}.

blunt.li: {PAWN_nameDef} told the visitors from {FACTION} where to rest and where to eat, and left them to it.

cheerful.li: {PAWN_nameDef} had {OTHER_nameDef} of {FACTION} laughing within the hour, and the rest of the visitors soon after.

cold.li: {PAWN_nameDef} received the visitors from {FACTION} with every courtesy, and took note of what each of them asked about.

plain.li: {PAWN_nameDef}, one of the colony's elders, spent the afternoon showing {OTHER_nameDef} what {PAWN_pronoun} knows of {SKILL}, the slow way, by doing it together.
{PAWN_nameDef} watched {OTHER_nameDef} at {SKILL} for a while without a word, then took over and showed {OTHER_objective} the trick of it.
{PAWN_nameDef} told {OTHER_nameDef} how {PAWN_pronoun} learned {SKILL}, mistakes and all, and then made {OTHER_objective} make the same mistakes on purpose.
[lowtech] {PAWN_nameDef} taught {OTHER_nameDef} the old way of {SKILL}, the way {PAWN_pronoun} was taught it as a child.

warm.li: {PAWN_nameDef} took {OTHER_nameDef} under {PAWN_possessive} wing for an afternoon of {SKILL}, and said "again" as kindly the tenth time as the first.

blunt.li: {PAWN_nameDef} showed {OTHER_nameDef} how {SKILL} is really done, twice, and then left {OTHER_objective} to get on with it.

cold.li: {PAWN_nameDef} stood over {OTHER_nameDef} through an afternoon of {SKILL} and corrected every mistake, without once raising {PAWN_possessive} voice.

plain.li: {PAWN_nameDef}, one of the colony's elders, told {OTHER_nameDef} stories from before the colony, about the places {PAWN_pronoun} lived and the people who are gone.
{PAWN_nameDef} sat with {OTHER_nameDef} on the step and talked about how things were, and how they might be.

warm.li: {PAWN_nameDef} asked {OTHER_nameDef} what {OTHER_pronoun} wanted from life, and listened to all of it.

gloomy.li: {PAWN_nameDef} told {OTHER_nameDef} about the people {PAWN_pronoun} has outlived. {OTHER_nameDef} listened to every name.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} spent the afternoon with me. I got more from listening to {OTHER_objective} than from a month on my own.
{OTHER_nameDef} told me I was doing it wrong and showed me why. From {OTHER_objective}, I don't mind.
Sat with {OTHER_nameDef} after work. I'd heard two of the stories before and let {OTHER_objective} tell them anyway.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} said I reminded {OTHER_objective} of someone {OTHER_pronoun} used to know. I think it was a compliment.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} taught me a trick today and I've done it eleven times since!

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} won't be with us forever. I'm trying to learn everything while I can.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} has forgotten more than most of us know. Worth an afternoon.
